questions.stem: Why do simple covalent molecules have low melting and boiling points?

options.text: Because the covalent bonds within the molecules are weak
Because the intermolecular forces between the molecules are weak
Because the molecules are very large
Because they contain ions that are easily separated

questions.explanation: Simple covalent molecules have low melting and boiling points because the intermolecular forces (forces between molecules) are weak and require little energy to overcome. The covalent bonds within each molecule are strong but are not broken during melting or boiling.

questions.stem: Why do simple covalent molecules not conduct electricity?

options.text: Because they have no overall charge and no free electrons or ions to carry charge
Because their bonds are too strong

questions.explanation: Simple covalent molecules cannot conduct electricity because they have no free electrons or ions to carry electrical charge. The electrons are all held in covalent bonds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a simple covalent molecule?
questions.explanation: Methane (CH₄) is a simple covalent molecule consisting of one carbon atom covalently bonded to four hydrogen atoms. NaCl is ionic, diamond is giant covalent, and copper is metallic.

questions.stem: What are the weak forces between simple covalent molecules called?
questions.explanation: The weak forces of attraction between simple covalent molecules are called intermolecular forces. These are much weaker than the covalent bonds within the molecules themselves.

questions.stem: As the size of simple covalent molecules increases, what happens to their boiling points?
questions.explanation: Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces because they have more electrons and a greater surface area. This means more energy is needed to separate them, so boiling points increase.

questions.stem: What happens to the covalent bonds when a simple molecular substance melts?

options.text: The covalent bonds remain intact; only intermolecular forces are overcome
The covalent bonds become ionic bonds

questions.explanation: When a simple molecular substance melts, only the weak intermolecular forces between molecules are overcome. The strong covalent bonds within each molecule are not broken.

questions.stem: Which of these substances would you expect to be a gas at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen (H₂) is a small simple covalent molecule with very weak intermolecular forces, so it has an extremely low boiling point and is a gas at room temperature.
